questions.prompt: Which choice combines all three sentences into one cumulative sentence with a main clause followed by coordinated verb phrases in the original order? The robotics team unpacked the new laptops. It tested each device. It labeled the storage boxes.
choices: The robotics team, while testing each device, unpacked the new laptops and labeled the storage boxes.
After the robotics team unpacked the new laptops, it tested each device and labeled the storage boxes.
The robotics team unpacked the new laptops, and it tested each device; it labeled the storage boxes.
The robotics team unpacked the new laptops, tested each device, and labeled the storage boxes.
questions.explanation: The sentence begins with one main clause and then adds three parallel action phrases in the order given by the source sentences.

questions.prompt: The Red Maple is a community center. Its language classes focus on conversational skills. Its kitchen serves evening meals. Which choice uses an appositive to identify The Red Maple and a relative clause to modify language classes?
choices: The Red Maple is a community center, and it has language classes that focus on conversational skills, while its kitchen serves evening meals.
The Red Maple, which is a community center, has language classes focusing on conversational skills, and its kitchen serves evening meals.
The Red Maple, a community center, has language classes that focus on conversational skills, and its kitchen serves evening meals.
The Red Maple, a community center whose classes focus on conversational skills, has a kitchen serving evening meals.
questions.explanation: The appositive a community center identifies The Red Maple, and the relative clause that focus on conversational skills directly modifies language classes.

questions.prompt:
Combine the three sentences into one periodic sentence that begins with two separate introductory subordinate clauses and ends with a main clause:
The fire alarm sounded. The students evacuated the building. The teachers checked the rolls.
choices: The teachers checked the rolls after the fire alarm sounded and the students evacuated the building.
The fire alarm sounded, the students evacuated the building, and the teachers checked the rolls.
After the fire alarm sounded, the students evacuated the building; then the teachers checked the rolls.
When the fire alarm sounded, after the students evacuated the building, the teachers checked the rolls.
questions.explanation: The correct option opens with two subordinate clauses (“When…”, “after…”) before the main clause, forming a periodic structure.

questions.prompt: Elena repaired the radio. The radio was on the kitchen shelf. Elena found a loose wire. Which sentence combines all three details and uses an it-cleft to emphasize Elena as the person who performed the repair?
choices: It was the radio that Elena, after finding a loose wire, repaired on the kitchen shelf.
It was Elena who, after finding a loose wire, repaired the radio that was on the kitchen shelf.
Was it Elena who, after finding a loose wire, repaired the radio that was on the kitchen shelf?
It was on the kitchen shelf that Elena repaired the radio after finding a loose wire.
questions.explanation: The it-cleft foregrounds Elena as the agent of the repair, while the subordinate clauses retain the loose wire and the radio's kitchen-shelf location.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with an it-cleft construction
questions.topic: Combine Three Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence combines all three facts, retains the negative adverb Never, and correctly uses subject-auxiliary inversion? The observatory never opened before sunrise. The technicians unlocked the dome. The first stargazers arrived.
choices: Never the observatory had opened before sunrise, with the technicians unlocking the dome as the first stargazers arrived.
Never had the observatory opened before sunrise, with the technicians unlocking the dome as the first stargazers arrived.
Seldom had the observatory opened before sunrise, with the technicians unlocking the dome as the first stargazers arrived.
Never had the observatory open before sunrise, with the technicians unlocking the dome as the first stargazers arrived.
questions.explanation: The fronted negative adverb Never triggers subject-auxiliary inversion, and the with-phrase adds the entrance and visitor details.

questions.prompt: Which one-sentence explanation best describes the relationship between the clauses in this sentence? Although rehearsal had ended, the actors stayed to review their lines.
